mechanism_narrative: The residential stay-at-home premium is exhausting itself: RESIDENTIAL eased from 19.9 in t-1w to 19.0 in t-0w while TRANSIT stopped falling (-33.7 to -32.7). This joint exhaustion of the mobility retreat releases household time back into out-of-home channels, so RETAIL_REC drifts above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL peaked at 19.9 at t-1w and eased to 19.0 at t-0w
fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.7 at t-1w to -32.7 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with mobility floor forming
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to -22.95 (the last-28-day mean) in instances where RESIDENTIAL eases week-on-week and TRANSIT stops declining.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT reversing a two-week slide with a week-on-week gain of at least 1.0 point marks the establishment of a mobility floor; commuter volume then rebuilds and pulls weekday retail footfall upward, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the reversal.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain of >= 1.0 point after two consecutive weekly declines
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell -32.6 to -33.7 then rose to -32.7, a +1.0 point reversal
fact:WORKPLACES fell -16.7 to -19.0 then rose to -18.0, a +1.0 point reversal
failure_condition: Occasions where TRANSIT reverses a two-week decline by at least 1.0 point are followed by a next-14-day RETAIL_REC mean at or below the prior-14-day mean in more than half of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility held at 19.0 while WORKPLACES remains at -18.0 keeps the daytime population anchored at home and channels household spend toward essentials; discretionary retail is crowded out, so RETAIL_REC stays below its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL >= 15 and WORKPLACES <= -15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL averaged 19.0 and WORKPLACES -18.0 at t-0w, while GROCERY_PHARM held at +1.1
regime_hint: work-from-home and capacity restrictions in force
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL >= 15 and WORKPLACES <= -15, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the prior-28-day mean in more than half of the observed cases.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounding from its -20.6 trough at t-2w to -11.1 and -11.0 shows households re-engaging with out-of-home activity; under partial reopening this outdoor re-engagement leads discretionary retail by roughly two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS recovers at least 8 points from a trough within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -20.6 at t-2w to -11.1 at t-1w and -11.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Under partial reopening, a PARKS recovery of 8 or more points off a two-week trough is followed by a next-14-day RETAIL_REC mean at or below the prior-14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Deep suppression in TRANSIT (-32.7) and WORKPLACES (-18.0) with RESIDENTIAL pinned near +19 is the signature of active capacity caps and work-from-home direction; while these caps persist, discretionary trips are not substituted, so RETAIL_REC's next four weeks stay below the last four.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all four weekly TRANSIT readings are below -27 and all four RESIDENTIAL readings are above +16
regime_hint: legally binding capacity caps and work-from-home orders
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -25 and RESIDENTIAL above +15 yet the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds -22.95, the policy-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed within plus or minus 2 points of baseline in the last two weeks (1.4, 1.1), showing demand is not being siphoned into panic essentials; with essential-channel pull absent, marginal discretionary spending returns to retail within a single week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within +/-2 points of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM readings are 1.6, -1.6, 1.4, 1.1, i.e. within +/-2 of baseline in three of four weeks
failure_condition: Weeks with GROCERY_PHARM inside plus or minus 2 of baseline for two consecutive weeks are followed by a lower 7-day mean RETAIL_REC in more than half of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The 14-point week-on-week swing in PARKS (-6.4 to -20.6 to -11.1) reflects the onset of the year-end wet season; recurring rain suppresses outdoor trips and the retail footfall that co-locates with them, holding RETAIL_REC flat to lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS posts a week-on-week swing of >= 8 points in either direction
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved -6.4, -20.6, -11.1 across three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If the next-14-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds its prior-14-day mean while PARKS continues to swing 8 or more points week-on-week, the weather-suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Synchronised weekly easing of RESIDENTIAL (19.9 to 19.0) and WORKPLACES (-19.0 to -18.0) is a joint exit from the stay-home state rather than noise; when both improve in the same week, RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks as routine trips resume.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by >= 0.5 and WORKPLACES rises by >= 0.5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w RESIDENTIAL eased -0.9 and WORKPLACES rose +1.0 versus t-1w
failure_condition: Joint same-week improvement of RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES fails to precede a higher next-14-day RETAIL_REC mean in more than half of observed instances.
